proposal.summary: The problem is that IBAN format errors in refund processing cause failed refunds, which generate customer inquiries perceived as long wait times, even though actual agent response time is within SLA. This was established by evidence of five IBAN‑format refund failures (E-02), a median ticket response time of 2.0 h well below the 24 h SLA (E-01), and stakeholder reports of perceived long wait times (E-03). The released scope includes the action to notify customers of refund status to address perceived wait time. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the gate gave a CONDITIONAL_PASS, releasing the symptom‑addressing notification while deferring the root‑cause IBAN format validation; the released scope reduces perceived wait time but does not fix the IBAN errors shown in E-02. Known limitations are: DEFINE Gate CONDITIONAL_PASS (deferred items tracked as VOBs); semantic: semantic:Root problem coverage: Release scope only notifies customers; does not include IBAN format validation that prevents failed refunds, which is the root cause per evidence (E-02); VOB-U-U1 open; blocking_scope outside release scope; unfinished: scan_iban_format:payment-db (blocked by VOB-U-U1 until resolved: Will correcting IBAN format errors reduce inquiry volume and perceived wait time?).
key_points: Problem: IBAN format errors cause failed refunds leading to perceived long wait times (E-02, E-01, E-03).
Established via failure count, response time, and stakeholder claims (E-02, E-01, E-03).
Released: customer notification of refund status.
Decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION – gate CONDITIONAL_PASS, symptom treatment released, root cause deferred (E-02).
Limitations: gate conditional pass, missing IBAN validation (E-02), open VOB-U-U1, unfinished IBAN scan.
limitations_explained: The release does not include IBAN format validation, which evidence shows is the root cause of failed refunds (E-02).
The IBAN format scan remains deferred in VOB-U-U1, blocking the full solution.
Thus the release addresses only the symptom of perceived wait time, not the underlying IBAN errors.
